articles.title: One dependency for logs, traces and metrics: writing a Spring Boot starter
articles.excerpt: The worst time to discover that your services log differently is during an incident. It happens easily: each service is set up by a different person at a different time, so you end up with different f…
articles.body: The worst time to discover that your services log differently is during an incident. It happens easily: each service is set up by a different person at a different time, so you end up with different field names, trace IDs in some services but not others, and a correlation ID that stops at the first hop. In a platform with several services I've worked on, the answer was a shared module for logging, auth and tracing; this starter is that idea rebuilt in the open. The fix isn't a wiki page of conventions. It's making the right setup the default by putting it in a dependency. That's what spring-boot-starter-observability does: add one dependency to a Spring Boot 3 app and you get: Structured JSON logs with traceId , spanId , requestId and correlationId on every line.

articles.title: A container per task fixes isolation, and leaves the user waiting 45 seconds
articles.excerpt: The previous post ended here: with every task crammed into one program, one failure takes down all of them, and anybody's code can read everybody's data and keys. The fix is natural — give every task…
articles.body: The previous post ended here: with every task crammed into one program, one failure takes down all of them, and anybody's code can read everybody's data and keys. The fix is natural — give every task a container of its own . Throw it away afterwards; nobody touches anybody. On Kubernetes this is almost embarrassingly easy to write. Easy enough to make you wonder whether the last post was overreacting. The code: a task arrives, a container gets built # request comes in → ask K8s to build a new container v1 . create_namespaced_pod ( namespace = "default" , body = pod_manifest ) # then keep asking "ready yet? ready yet?" — this is the wait the user sits through while True : pod = v1 . read_namespaced_pod ( name = task_id , namespace = "default" ) if pod . status .

articles.title: IVR Full Form and Meaning: What Is an IVR Call?
articles.excerpt: "Press 1 for sales" is the most familiar phone UX there is, and one of the most disliked. If you're building or replacing one, it helps to know what an IVR actually does, when you need one at all, and…
articles.body: "Press 1 for sales" is the most familiar phone UX there is, and one of the most disliked. If you're building or replacing one, it helps to know what an IVR actually does, when you need one at all, and which kind fits. The IVR full form is Interactive Voice Response. An IVR is an automated phone system that answers a call, plays recorded or computer-read prompts, and acts on what the caller presses or says. It can give an answer itself, such as an order status, or connect the caller to the right person. This guide explains what an IVR call means if one just reached you. It also helps a business decide whether it needs an IVR, and which kind fits. Note: Key takeaways IVR means Interactive Voice Response. IVRS is the same thing, with "System" added at the end.

articles.body: TITLE: 대분해의 시대: 레이어 2가 블록체인의 핵심 약속을 재정의하는 방식 탈중앙화된 분산원장 시스템이라는 개념을 처음 접했을 때, 비트코인 설계의 순수한 우아함은 그야말로 매력적이었다. 중앙 권한 없이 네트워크 참여자들이 유지하는 전 세계적인 불변의 데이터베이스라니, 정말 강력한 비전이었다. 하지만 이런 단일체적 설계의 실질적인 한계가 드러나는 데는 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않았다. 초창기 블록 크기 논쟁을 기억한다. 전 세계적으로 복제되고, 안전하며, 탈중앙화된 원장이 광범위한 채택에 필요한 트랜잭션 처리량을 동시에 처리할 수 없다는 사실이 얼마나 빨리 명확해졌는지 말이다. 이것은 단순히 확장성 문제가 아니었다. 블록체인 아키텍처의 심장부에 있는 근본적인 긴장이었고, 지금도 그러하다. 수년 동안 우리는 비탈릭 부테린 같은 인물들이 대중화한 '블록체인 트릴레마'와 씨름해 왔다. 블록체인은 탈중앙화, 보안, 확장성 세 가지 속성 중 어느 한 시점에 두 가지만 달성할 수 있다는 개념이다. 초기 레이어 1 설계는 탈중앙화와 보안을 우선시했고, 필연적으로 확장성을 희생했다. 이더리움에서 수요가 폭증하는 기간에 이런 현상이 극적으로 나타났고, 트랜잭션 수수료는 수백 달러까지 치솟아 많은 사용자에게 기본적인 운영조차 엄청나게 비싼 일이 되기 일쑤였다. 2021년 8월, 아비트럼 원 메인넷 출시 등은 이런 병목 현상에 대한 직접적인 대응이었다. 이는 연산이 기반 레이어의 합의 메커니즘과 분리되는 미래를 엿보게 했다. 내 생각에 이것이야말로 레이어 2가 해결하고자 하는 핵심 질문이다.

articles.title: The Great Unbundling: How Layer 2s Are Redefining Blockchain's Core Promise
articles.excerpt: TITLE: The Great Unbundling: How Layer 2s Are Redefining Blockchain's Core Promise When I first encountered the concept of a decentralized ledger system, the sheer elegance of Bitcoin's design was cap…
articles.body: TITLE: The Great Unbundling: How Layer 2s Are Redefining Blockchain's Core Promise When I first encountered the concept of a decentralized ledger system, the sheer elegance of Bitcoin's design was captivating. A global, immutable database, maintained by a network of participants without any central authority. It was a powerful vision. But it didn't take long for the practical limitations of this monolithic design to surface. I remember the early debates about block size, and how quickly it became clear that a globally replicated, secure, and decentralized ledger couldn't simultaneously handle the transaction throughput needed for widespread adoption. This wasn't merely a scaling problem; it was, and remains, a fundamental tension at the heart of blockchain architecture.

articles.title: Can AI check your maths proofs? Yes, if you ask it the right question
articles.excerpt: AI is good enough to check most undergraduate maths exercises, but only if you ask it a narrow question. If you paste a proof and ask "is this correct?", the model will quite often say yes, tidy up yo…
articles.body: AI is good enough to check most undergraduate maths exercises, but only if you ask it a narrow question. If you paste a proof and ask "is this correct?", the model will quite often say yes, tidy up your wording and hand it back. You read the tidy version, it looks fine, and the gap is still there. So I'd ask something narrower: "Quote the first line that doesn't follow from the lines before it, and say what's missing." That gives you one specific thing to fix. It also stops the model rewriting the proof for you, which is the version you'd be tempted to just read and accept. Test it on a proof you've broken on purpose Before you trust any checker, give it something you know is wrong and see whether it notices.

articles.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has moved its Starship Super Heavy booster to the pad to prep for the next test flight of the megarocket, a historic mission scheduled to launch this Friday (Nov. 13).
articles.body: SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount.

articles.body: In any respectable audiobook project, finding the names of Andy Weir ("The Martian," "Project Hail Mary") and Benjamin Percy ("The Ninth Metal," "Wolverine") attached would elicit intense fan interest, but add the superstar vocal talents of Anthony Mackie ("Avengers: Infinity War," "Avengers: Doomsday"), Ariana DeBose ("West Side Story"), and John Leguizamo ("Ice Age"), and it catapults this sonic odyssey into the stratosphere. Such is the case with " Exoplanet ," Audible Original’s new 7-episode science fiction audio drama executive produced by Weir and penned by Percy. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected.

articles.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
articles.excerpt: Researcher finds 35,000 Grok Build apps wide open to anyone who looked for them.
articles.body: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it.
